title: The Fox in the Ice
author: Aesop (adapted by J. H. Stickney)
summary: 狐狸舍不得拽断冻住的尾巴，越等越牢，最后被狼一口咬掉。
publicDomainBasis: Aesop's fables are ancient; this retelling by J. H. Stickney was published in 1915. Published before 1923 and therefore public domain in the United States; Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: VERY early one winter morning, during a hard frost, a Fox was drinking at a hole in the ice not far from the haunts of men.
paragraphs.zh: 一个寒冬的清晨，天寒地冻，一只狐狸在人烟不远处的冰窟窿边喝水。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, whether by accident or from negligence does not matter, the end of its tail got wet and froze to the ice.
paragraphs.zh: 这时，不知是意外还是疏忽，它的尾巴尖沾了水，冻在了冰上。

paragraphs.en: No great harm was done; the Fox could easily remedy it. It had only to give a tolerably hard pull and leave about a score of hairs behind; then it could run home quickly before any one came.
paragraphs.zh: 这不算什么大祸，狐狸很容易补救。它只要使劲一拽，留下二十来根毛，就能趁没人来之前赶紧跑回家。

paragraphs.en: But how could it make up its mind to spoil its tail? Such a bushy tail as it was—so ample, so golden! No; better wait a little. Surely men are sleeping still. It is even possible that a thaw may set in meanwhile. In that case it will be able to withdraw its tail easily from the ice hole.
paragraphs.zh: 可它怎么舍得弄坏自己的尾巴呢？那么蓬松的一条尾巴——那么丰满，那么金黄！不行，还是再等一会儿。人们肯定还在睡觉。说不定这期间还会解冻。那样它就能轻松地把尾巴从冰窟窿里抽出来了。

paragraphs.en: So it waits; it goes on waiting, but its tail only freezes all the more. The Fox looks round; the day is already beginning to dawn. People are stirring; voices are to be heard. Our poor Fox begins to move wildly about, now this way and now that. But still it cannot free itself from the hole.
paragraphs.zh: 于是它等着；等啊等，尾巴却只是越冻越牢。狐狸四下张望，天已经开始亮了。人们起身了，能听见说话声。可怜的狐狸开始发疯似的东奔西窜，可还是没法从冰窟窿里挣脱。

paragraphs.en: Luckily, a Wolf comes running that way.
paragraphs.zh: 幸好，一只狼正好从那儿跑过。

paragraphs.en: “Dear friend! father!” cries the Fox; “do save me; I am all but lost!”
paragraphs.zh: “亲爱的朋友！老父亲！”狐狸叫道，“救救我吧，我快没命了！”

paragraphs.en: So the Wolf stopped and set to work to rescue the Fox. Its method was a simple one—it bit the tail clean off.
paragraphs.zh: 狼停下脚步，动手救狐狸。它的办法很简单——一口把尾巴咬断。

paragraphs.en: So our foolish friend went home tailless, but rejoicing that its skin was still on its back.
paragraphs.zh: 于是我们这位愚蠢的朋友没了尾巴回家去，却庆幸自己的皮还留在背上。
